title: Entropy-aware scheduler + prober for FlashAttention v3 to stabilize prefill/decode latency
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Since we started rolling out FlashAttention v3 variants to some clusters, we've observed intermittent decode latency oscillations during steady-state burst traffic. These manifest as 50-300ms spikes affecting tail latency SLOs for multi-turn chat routes. Symptoms appear correlated with prefill+decode handoffs where the kernel selector flips between v2-compatible and v3-optimized kernels under certain sequence-length/occupancy patterns.

Hypothesis: Oscillation is driven by two interacting factors: (1) telemetry-sparse kernel probing that reacts to transient noise (short bursts cause the prober to reinterpret signal as a persistent shift) and (2) v3 kernel runtime sensitivity to cache/tiling decisions exposing a bifurcation point where small changes in prefix length or occupancy push the runtime between two kernel families. The combined effect creates a feedback loop that amplifies transient workload jitter.

Goal: Reduce tail latency jitter for affected routes without materially increasing average latency or cost. Provide a safe rollout path and monitoring/alerting to catch regressions early.

Success criteria (acceptance):
- 95th and 99th latency for decode tokens on affected routes reduced to within 10% of baseline (pre-v3 rollout), measured over 72h window.
- Kernel-selector oscillation rate (switches per 5m window) reduced by >80% in canaries.
- No >2% increase in average token cost for canary traffic.

Plan of work:
1) Implement an "entropy-aware prefill scheduler" that smooths kernel-probe input by measuring short-window entropy of recent sequence lengths and occupancy; high-entropy windows suppress immediate prober decisions and apply a fractional slew rate to kernel score updates.
2) Add a lightweight prober damping component: when prober flips occur more than N times in T seconds for a particular model-version, apply exponential backoff to probing and bias routing toward the safer kernel family for a cooldown period.
3) Expand telemetry: new metrics (kernel_selector_choice, kernel_switch_count, selector_score_v2, selector_score_v3, sequence_entropy, occupancy_histogram) and add tagging by route/model/shard. Dashboards + alerts in Datadog.
4) Offline experiments: run synthetic replay of representative workloads (chat short-turns, long-context summarization, embeddings-heavy prefix) on a small farm to validate threshold choices.
5) Canary rollout: phased canary starting with 1% of low-risk routes -> 5% -> 20% with automatic rollback triggers on latency or oscillation thresholds.
6) Post-rollout: small traffic retention test (48-72h) and long-tail regression guardrail.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive damping reduces oscillation but risks being slow to adapt to genuine workload shifts. We plan param sweeps (backoff base, cooldown window) to find a balance.
- Smoothing will add some decision lag which could marginally increase average latency; our acceptance criteria allows small average cost/latency changes.

Artifacts / links in ticket: Confluence design doc and datadog dashboards + PRs are linked in comments below.

Rollout and backout: Canary automation will evaluate the three primary indicators (95th/99th decode latency, kernel_switch_count, avg token cost). If any trigger breaches, we auto-fall back to the previous stable selector policy and open an incident for follow-up.

Owners: Runtime team (lead: Tom Nguyen), Telemetry (support: Marta Ruiz), QA (support: Ben Carter).
